paper_title: Towards Predicting Any Human Trajectory In Context
caption: Performance of random example selection and the proposed STES at varying numbers of in-context examples with a larger number of examples

model_annotations.English: The plot illustrates the performance of two methods—ST-ES (proposed method) and Random example selection—measured by the minADE₂₀ metric, as a function of the number of in-context examples, ranging from 0 to 15. The x-axis, labeled "Number of Examples," uses a linear scale with integer tick marks from 0 to 15 at regular intervals of 5. The y-axis, labeled "minADE₂₀ (←)", also uses a linear scale, ranging from 15.00 to 17.00, with tick marks every 0.50 units. The blue line with circular markers represents ST-ES; it starts at a high value of 17.00 at 0 examples, drops sharply to approximately 15.10 at 1 example, then continues to decrease more gradually to around 14.75 at 5 examples, stabilizing near 14.70 to 14.80 from 8 to 15 examples with minor fluctuations. The orange line with circular markers represents the Random method; it begins at approximately 16.70 at 0 examples and remains relatively flat, hovering between 16.45 and 16.50 across all example counts from 1 to 15, indicating minimal improvement with increasing examples.
model_annotations.German: The plot illustrates the performance of two example selection methods—ST-ES (proposed method) and Random—measured by the minADE₂₀ metric, as the number of in-context examples varies from 0 to 15. The x-axis, labeled "Number of Examples," is linear and ranges from 0 to 15, with tick marks at intervals of 5. The y-axis, labeled "minADE₂₀ (→)", is also linear and ranges from 15.00 to 17.00, with tick marks at intervals of 0.50. The ST-ES method is represented by a blue line with circular markers; it starts at approximately 17.00 when the number of examples is 0, drops sharply to about 15.10 at 1 example, and then remains relatively stable around 14.90 to 15.00 for 2 to 15 examples. The Random method is shown by an orange line with circular markers; it begins at approximately 16.70 at 0 examples, decreases slightly to about 16.50 at 1 example, and then stays nearly constant around 16.50 to 16.60 across 2 to 15 examples. The legend in the upper right corner identifies the two lines, and the plot includes a grid for easier value estimation.
